findings.title: Pull-request builds gain access to shared internal runners
findings.summary: A contributor whose pull-request workflow is permitted can execute modified build/test or local-action code on the project's self-hosted runners, gaining their internal network and shared local build state. The source explicitly places these runners on a private Docker network with a tokenless shared cache.

severity.rationale: The boundary crosses from a fork contribution into the internal runner environment. The attacker can execute arbitrary job code and contact the documented private cache; persistence, cache poisoning and access to other services depend on deployment details not established by source. GitHub approval settings may require a maintainer to permit the run.
severity.changeConditions: Reduce severity if PR jobs are proven to use disposable runners with no shared state or internal network; raise it if persistent credentials or a writable cache consumed by trusted builds are confirmed.

confidence.rationale: Workflow scheduling, attacker-controlled checkout and internal cache endpoint are explicit in current source; live runner isolation and Actions approval policy were not inspected.

codeEvidence.label: Shared unauthenticated internal cache
codeEvidence.code:
# The self-hosted runners share one mbx cache server on their private Docker
# network (`mbx-cache`), so a crate one runner compiled is a cache hit on the
# others. The server takes no token: mbx sends none over plain HTTP, and only
# the runners can reach it. mbx publishes only from pushes to a protected
# branch; pull requests read. GitHub-hosted runners cannot reach the server,
# so jobs that also run there keep Swatinem/rust-cache on those legs.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - uses: jdx/mr-boxington-action@47ce49b32025d93a7a2f4570815afaa2b7092240 # v1.7.2
      with:
        backend: remote
        version: "1.24.1"
        remote-url: http://mbx-cache:7543
        namespace: jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines
codeEvidence.explanation: Shared unauthenticated internal cache

rootCause.summary: The `pull_request` trigger schedules the checked-out contribution on `self-hosted` without a trusted-origin guard. The local `.github/actions/mbx` action and Cargo/test/script commands run with the runner account and its network access. The private-network restriction described for `mbx-cache` does not distinguish PR code from trusted jobs once both execute on these runners.

findings.remediation: Run all untrusted pull-request jobs on fresh isolated hosted runners, or enforce disposable self-hosted sandboxes with no trusted shared state, internal service access or reusable credentials. Restrict internal runner jobs to explicitly trusted events and enforce cache write authorization on the server.

counterEvidence: Job tokens have contents:read and checkout persist-credentials:false; neither removes host/network authority from arbitrary job code.
GitHub may require approval before running an external contributor's job.
No live host, cache service, credential or network access was attempted; cache poisoning is not claimed as demonstrated.
limitations: Runner lifecycle, fork run policy and cache server-side authorization are unavailable in the authorized source.
validation.summary: Checked all self-hosted PR workflow families and their job guards. Source establishes no origin restriction in CI/docs/adoption/roundtrip, while the shared action documents and configures private HTTP cache access.

dataflow.summary: pull_request source -> actions/checkout -> local composite action / Cargo tests / repository scripts -> internal runner process and mbx-cache network
dataflow.sink: self-hosted runner account and private Docker network
dataflow.outcome: An external contributor gains execution inside the internal CI trust zone.

reachability.summary: Requires a PR run to be enabled or approved. No repository write privilege, release credential, or existing internal-network access is required to author a fork PR.
reachability.entrypoint: pull_request jobs in CI, Docs, Markdown round trip and adoption
reachability.outcome: Arbitrary execution with the CI runner's network and filesystem authority
preconditions: Self-hosted runners are registered and PR workflows are permitted by GitHub settings.

attackPath.summary: Submit a PR changing a local action, build hook or test; when its workflow runs, that code executes on `self-hosted` and can access the runner's private network and shared build state.

remediationTests: Assert every pull_request job is routed to an isolated runner pool or rejects untrusted head repositories.
Verify an untrusted build cannot reach the internal cache or read state from an earlier trusted job.
preventiveControls: Separate untrusted PR compute and trusted push/release infrastructure.

findings.title: Rendering an HTML table with a large colspan exhausts memory
findings.summary: Render a DOCX containing an internal HTML/MHT `w:altChunk` with one table cell whose `colspan` is `4294967295`. The converter accepts it as `usize` and tries to append billions of grid-column elements before layout, exhausting process memory or CPU despite a tiny admitted package.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can deterministically force enormous allocation and work through normal conversion. This can terminate a native host process, Python/MCP server or WASM instance; no remote deployment is assumed. The repository recommends process CPU/memory limits, which contain host damage but do not make the conversion succeed.
severity.changeConditions: Shared service exposure increases operational impact; disposable conversion workers with enforced memory/CPU limits reduce collateral impact.

confidence.rationale: The source directly converts an unbounded parsed integer into a counted String-append loop before any page raster bound. No runtime reproduction was run.

rootCause.summary: `with_layout` admits the original package then expands its internal altChunk. `Builder::start` accepts a cell span with only a lower bound. `end_table` sums spans into a column count and allocates one XML grid column for every claimed column. preventiveControls: Apply resource limits to decoded/expanded representations, not only archive bytes.

findings.title: Imported CSS selector lists multiply memory during rendering
findings.summary: A DOCX HTML/MHT altChunk can put thousands of distinct selectors before one large property value. The importer clones that entire String-backed declaration map for every selector, retaining gigabytes from about a megabyte of HTML before any body content needs to use those rules.

severity.rationale: Attacker-supplied document content reaches an eager allocation sink in public rendering. Thousands of independent copies can exhaust the CLI or an embedding process; a shared service is not assumed. Caller process limits contain the failed conversion but do not bound its expansion.
severity.changeConditions: Dedicated memory-limited workers reduce collateral damage; concurrent shared rendering increases availability impact.

confidence.rationale: Props is a String-valued map and the selector loop explicitly clones it; html_to_wml eagerly parses the full style block. No dynamic allocation test was run.

findings.title: Malformed WMF text records exhaust memory while rendering
findings.summary: Render a document with an embedded placeable WMF containing many small text records whose character counts extend into later records. The renderer accepts each range if it fits the file and retains a separate decoded String, allowing less than 1MiB of media to request roughly 4GiB of text storage.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can trigger the WMF parser through embedded drawings and exhaust the host process without large admitted input. The effect is availability loss; no memory corruption or file disclosure is claimed. SECURITY.md recommends caller process limits, which contain collateral damage.
severity.changeConditions: Memory-limited disposable conversion workers reduce collateral damage; a long-lived shared embedding host increases operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Both text handlers use whole-file ranges despite the record-length check, and every accepted range becomes independently retained String text. The overlapping-range construction is supported statically; no exploit execution.

rootCause.summary: Embedded drawing bytes flow through decode_image into the placeable WMF decoder. The iterator checks a declared record size against remaining file bytes but leaves payload readers pointed at the full file. EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT accept counts extending beyond that record. wmf_text decodes every overlapping span into an independent String and the outer texts vector retains them all.

findings.remediation: Parse each WMF record from a slice confined to its declared extent, validate every text/padding/rectangle/coordinate length against that slice, and enforce an aggregate decoded-text and work budget.

counterEvidence: checked_mul prevents size/iterator wrap, not cross-record reads.
Each n is u16-bounded; multiplicative aggregate retention remains.
384-pixel canvas cap and stroke clipping do not limit texts.
Sibling EMF point parsing uses record bounds; this finding concerns the two WMF text branches.
limitations: Actual OOM threshold and UTF8 size vary by host/bytes; no runtime reproduction.
validation.summary: A 7-word EXTTEXTOUT record contains its 6-byte header and 8-byte fixed fields but can declare 65535 text bytes starting at the next record. Repeating 65536 such 14-byte records plus a 65535-byte suffix keeps every range inside a file under 1MiB while causing ~4GiB of separately decoded characters. Nonzero placeable dimensions pass the geometry guard.

dataflow.summary: embedded a:blip -> resolve_media -> decode_image -> metafile::render -> raster_wmf -> full-file text ranges -> MetaText Strings
dataflow.outcome: large retained allocation and CPU consumption

reachability.summary: A supplier of DOCX bytes controls embedded media accepted by public conversion APIs. No external image URL, filesystem write privilege or special renderer option is needed beyond selecting a document with a drawing.

attackPath.summary: Embed a WMF with many short EXTTEXTOUT or TEXTOUT records and oversized overlapping character spans, then request document rendering.

remediationTests: Refuse EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT whose counts or coordinate fields extend past their own record even when still inside the file.
Ensure many valid records hit a bounded aggregate text budget and ordinary WMF text stays supported.
preventiveControls: Pass bounded record slices to all metafile handlers instead of exposing the entire backing file.

findings.title: Nonstandard auxiliary part names bypass XML depth checks
findings.summary: A DOCX can point its styles, theme, numbering or font-table relationship to XML stored under a `.bin` name. Admission charges its bytes but skips XML depth/tag policy. Rendering resolves the relationship and recursively parses that unchecked XML, allowing a small deeply nested part to exhaust the host stack.

severity.rationale: Document suppliers control part names, relationships and contents at a public conversion boundary. A deeply nested auxiliary part can abort the CLI or embedding process, bypassing the documented depth=256 control. Archive byte bounds and recommended process limits constrain collateral damage, but not this stack-depth violation.
severity.changeConditions: Per-job disposable workers reduce service collateral damage; shared long-lived conversion hosts increase availability impact.

confidence.rationale: Admission's filename predicate, main-only exception, arbitrary relationship selection and unchecked recursive parser are explicit source; no runtime stack-overflow input was executed.

rootCause.summary: Package admission recognizes XML by `.xml`/`.rels` suffix and separately checks only a nonstandard main-document name. OPC auxiliary relationships are allowed arbitrary internal target names. Conversion opens those selected parts as text and calls permissive parse_xdocument, whose nested-element branch recurses without a depth check. Renaming the target changes admission classification without changing its later XML interpretation.

findings.remediation: Identify all XML by supported relationship/content types during admission and validate every selected XML part under the active InputLimits immediately before DOM construction, regardless of filename. Prefer checked parser APIs at these boundaries.

limitations: Crash depth depends on host stack/target; no dynamic reproduction.
